question: How do you create a hyperlink in HTML?
answer: To create a hyperlink in HTML, we use the <a> (anchor) tag. The most important attribute is href, which specifies the destination URL. The text or content between the opening and closing <a> tags becomes the clickable link. We can also use target="_blank" to open the link in a new tab.
code: Visit Google Visit Google About Us Send Email

question: What is the difference between absolute and relative URLs?
answer: Absolute URL: It is the complete address of a webpage or resource, including the protocol (https://) and domain name. Example: https://www.example.com/about.html. It works from anywhere. Relative URL: It is a partial path that is relative to the current page location. Example: about.html or /images/logo.png. Relative URLs are shorter and commonly used for linking pages within the same website.
code: Contact Contact Photo About (going one folder up)

question: How do you add an image in HTML? What attributes are important for images?
answer: To add an image, we use the tag (it is a void/self-closing element). The most important attributes are: src (path of the image), alt (alternative text), width and height (to set size), and title (tooltip text). Always include the alt attribute for accessibility and SEO.

question: What is the purpose of the alt attribute?
answer: The alt (alternative text) attribute provides a text description of the image. It is very important for: 1) Accessibility – screen readers read the alt text for visually impaired users, 2) SEO – search engines use alt text to understand the image, 3) Fallback – if the image fails to load, the alt text is displayed instead. Always write meaningful alt text that describes the image.

question: How do you make images responsive using HTML?
answer: To make images responsive (so they adjust according to screen size), the simplest way in HTML is to set the max-width to 100% and height to auto using CSS or the style attribute. This ensures the image never overflows its container and scales down on smaller screens. We can also use the <picture> element or srcset attribute for more advanced responsive images.
code: /* CSS */ .responsive-img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }
